problem: Prior social navigation methods struggle to perceive social context and comply with social norms in dense crowds, and end-to-end planners lack semantic understanding.
motivation: Robots in crowded human environments need both semantic social reasoning and reliable real-time collision avoidance. LLMs offer semantic understanding and decision-making, but are too slow and unreliable for low-level control, which motivates separating high-level planning from real-time control.
key_idea: Use an LLM for high-level semantic and social-factor reasoning and planning, and delegate real-time obstacle avoidance to an MPC controller.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablations can be cited. The claimed benefit comes from decoupling slow semantic LLM reasoning from fast MPC-based control, and from adding social factor analysis.
method: LLM high-level planner: performs semantic understanding and decision-making for navigation in crowds
Social factor analysis: integrates social cues and norms into the decisions
MPC controller: performs real-time obstacle avoidance and tracks the high-level plan
Hierarchical decoupling: separates high-level planning from low-level control
